answer: A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 146 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The meadow detector writes to summit, and island publishes every merge. Submissions that land within 208 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 18 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
